#28095. I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1649 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1649 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that in a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary.
  • Take Southwest Airlines, for example.
  • "Experiences create lifetime memories,” notes Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

Take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

"Experiences create lifetime memories,” notes Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”.

In a recent development, southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but major-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

According to recent reports, the event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:.

A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

It has been revealed that even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.).

Industry observers note that as of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

$1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.).

Four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.).

If you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

Recent findings suggest that using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

In a recent development, daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

Sources indicate that ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

It has been revealed that again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

It has been revealed that I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

Industry observers note that grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

The biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

You’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

It has been revealed that with that noted, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

It has been revealed that scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.).

Finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

Southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

But every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

Personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

"We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” states Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

Instead, you probably would've been interested in the 250,000-point package for "Boots, Bourbon and Bonfires" — a three-day trip to Devil's Thumb Ranch, an upscale dude ranch resort about 1.5 hours outside of Denver.

Before you book, just remember: You’ll need a Southwest credit card to purchase.

You want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s important to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

iOS 27.3 Could Bring the Redesigned Health App and a More Capable Siri AI to Your Device Soon

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that apple rolled out the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov.
  • Apple historically releases an iOS revision in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.
  • According to recent reports, since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple rolled out the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov. 19, more than two months after the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iOS 27. The headliner here is the return of the newly introduced Health app: After briefly testing the redesigned Health app in an early iOS 27.2 beta, Apple has put the revamped app back in the recent beta cycle.

Apple historically releases an iOS revision in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.

According to recent reports, since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.3, so the patch might be buggy and battery life may be short, so it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, there could be more features to land on your iPhone when Apple releases 27.3.

Here are some features developers and beta testers can try now in the second iOS 27.3 beta.

The redesigned Health app returns in the iOS 27.3 beta after Apple tested the feature in the iOS 27.2 beta process. Developers and beta testers can explore the refreshed app and see things like a new Longevity tab and your Health Age.

Apple wrote online that we can expect the redesigned Health app to land on devices later this year.

If developers and beta testers have an Apple Watch that is running the watchOS 27.3 beta as well as an iPhone running the iOS 27.3 beta, those folks can test out Apple’s Live Rewind and Siri Recap in Audio Intelligence.

Live Rewind allows you to pull up a text transcript of a conversation in the past 15 seconds on your Apple Watch, and Siri Recap can automatically give you a summary of meetings, conversations and other events. Live Rewind snippets are replaced by upcoming audio and then deleted, and Siri Recaps delete themselves after seven days if you don’t manually delete them sooner. However, you can also save both of these in the Siri app and export them to the Notes or Journal apps on your iPhone.

Recent findings suggest that while both Live Rewind and Siri Recap are automatically deleted over time, I’m uncomfortable with the ability to save snippets or recaps, which raises concerns about people recording my conversations without my knowledge. Even if Audio Intelligence just summarizes what I stated, I still find both features creepy.

And while I recognize the utility for certain groups of people, I also think it’s better to just, y’know… talk to someone instead of asking your watch what they just mentioned.

According to recent reports, siri AI gets a huge update in the iOS 27.3 beta. The feature can now do more actions in supported apps, like Apple Music and Messages. For example, if you go into Apple Music, you can ask Siri to create a playlist for you, and in Messages, you can ask Siri to schedule, edit or unsend messages. If you open an app and ask Siri what it can do, the digital assistant should give you some examples of its capabilities.

You can also use Siri in Safari to scan an entire webpage — even parts of the page that aren’t in your direct view — to give you helpful information. So if you are looking at a menu online, you can ask Siri to find the gluten-free or vegetarian options.

The beta also brings Siri AI to traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian.

In the latest iOS 27.3 beta, developers and beta testers can find video podcasts in the Apple TV app, as well as in the Podcasts app. You can find video podcasts by going into the app, tapping Home across the bottom of your screen and scrolling down to the Video Podcasts section.

This means you can watch a video podcast in the Apple TV app on your iPhone while commuting, and then you can finish that video later on an Apple TV 4K or another device with access to Apple TV.

Industry observers note that each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets and weights in order to help you meet your goals. And if you’re unfamiliar with an exercise, you can also watch video tutorials to see how to perform that exercise.

According to recent reports, standBy mode also gets an upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. In the beta, you can add full weather and calendar slides to the mode and choose from more colors.

Apple introduced StandBy mode alongside iOS 17, and it was one of my favorite iPhone features. I’m happy Apple is finally showing it some love and adding more features and capabilities so it feels more like a home or desk hub.

If you’re a fan of dark mode, the iOS 27.3 beta has a treat for you. The beta gives you a upcoming setting in Safari called Adaptive Dark Mode. When enabled, it forces dark mode onto webpages in Safari that may not have a dark mode option otherwise.

Here’s where to find the option.

1. Tap Settings.2. Tap Apps.3. Tap Safari.4. Tap Adaptive Dark Mode.5. Tap On.

If you have an iPhone Duo and are running the iOS 27.3 beta, you have new options to lock and unlock your device. In the beta, you can enable your device to lock simply by closing the Duo. You can find this option in Settings and within the Display & Brightness menu.

Sources indicate that next, people with the Duo can unlock the device using that phone’s front camera and without opening the foldable. You will have had to recently unlocked your device with Touch ID or your passcode. You can find this option in Settings and in the Touch ID & Passcode menu.

Recent findings suggest that those are a few of the latest features developers can try now with the second beta of iOS 27.3. Apple has not stated when exactly it will release iOS 27.3 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices before the end of the year.

For more iOS news, here’s what to know about iOS 27.2, why you may have missed iOS 27.1 and our iOS 27 cheat sheet.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release.
  • In a recent development, but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04?
  • Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

In a recent development, but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is presently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

It has been revealed that this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

According to recent reports, desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

One thing that surprised me is that Myna (Ubuntu’s AI dictation tool) has yet to find its way into the Ubuntu ISO as a default app. As with Ubuntu 26.10, you can install it, but you have to first add the necessary repository with:.

With the repository added, you can install it with:.

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

It’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

Among iOS 27’s many new features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

With iOS 27, Apple introduces major AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting new features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the update also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:.

It has been revealed that after iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

Sources indicate that to move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

In a recent development, most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

But the carriers don’t unless you pay them.

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you've ever struggled to keep a project organized or stay on top of a seemingly endless stream of emails, this could be one of the most useful ChatGPT upgrades yet.

Think of ChatGPT Space as a digital workspace that combines some of the best features of Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 and Notion with the intelligence of ChatGPT.

Rather than digging through old conversations to find something ChatGPT created, you can organize your work in one dedicated location.

At the heart of Space is a feature called Pages. These interactive documents can include text, images, charts, tables and even interactive tools. You can edit them yourself, ask ChatGPT to make changes or invite other people to collaborate.

You can also turn an existing ChatGPT conversation into a page without starting from scratch.

One of the biggest frustrations with using AI for productivity is that the information it generates can swiftly become outdated.

ChatGPT Space aims to solve that problem with automated document updates. You can tell ChatGPT what information to patch, which connected apps to consult and how frequently to check them.

A weekly family planner that incorporates school announcements and upcoming appointments.

A daily to-do list that pulls action items from your emails.

A vacation itinerary that reflects new booking confirmations.

A job search tracker that incorporates responses from potential employers.

A project dashboard that reflects the latest conversations in Slack.

Instead of repeatedly asking ChatGPT for the same information, you can return to an existing document to review what's changed.

OpenAI is also bringing ChatGPT Slides to Space. Powered in part by Imagegen 2.6, the feature lets you create polished presentations, collaborate with others and ask ChatGPT to incorporate feedback.

Additionally, ChatGPT generates editable charts rather than static chart images. You can modify individual elements, export your presentation to PowerPoint and edit the underlying chart data in Excel.

For anyone who's ever spent an entire afternoon tweaking a PowerPoint presentation, this alone could make Space worth exploring.

You can start with a blank page, choose a template or turn an existing conversation into a document.

Try giving ChatGPT a prompt like this: Create a weekly personal dashboard with my upcoming commitments, outstanding tasks and notable emails. Set it up to refresh every Monday morning using my connected apps.

You'll need to connect the relevant services and configure the recurring updates.

While much of the competition between ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude focuses on which AI model is smarter, Space now seems like a step toward making AI more useful in everyday life.

It has been revealed that I'm particularly interested in the potential for documents that stay current without requiring constant attention. As someone who uses AI every day, I rarely struggle to create a to-do list, research document or project strategy, but keeping it all organized is a different story. According to recent reports, some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving upgrade. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

In a recent development, the v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch customers can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

Also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s new model worth it?

Constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

In a recent development, wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how rapidly it can drain.

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future.

The update improves battery life without users having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

Recent findings suggest that that’s not the only Google Play Services update that Wear OS smartwatch users can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

According to recent reports, hyperscalers and chipmakers adopt dual vendor strategies (buying test equipment from two suppliers) to secure capacity and avoid supply chain delays. This approach speeds high-volume production for next-generation data center architectures.

Quarterly sales holding above $1.2 billion reflect a structural step change in operational scale. Teradyne expands manufacturing capacity and dual-sources component suppliers to meet artificial intelligence infrastructure demand.

Heavy research investments and open partner ecosystems protect technical leadership across test and robotics segments. Management watches customer qualification pacing and supply lead times as semiconductor capital spending expands through 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that flagship phones are the prized devices that pair bleeding-edge hardware with unmatched performance across the board. While the iPhone 18 Pro Max, Galaxy S26 Ultra, and Pixel 11 Pro XL lead the way as some of the best phones you can buy, you don't always need to spend $1,299 or more to get a top-tier experience. That’s why I'm turning my attention to their slightly more accessible siblings.

Recent findings suggest that I've spent months testing the iPhone 17, Galaxy S26, and Pixel 11, putting them through different matchups and photo face-offs — all to see how they perform against one another. Normally, these base flagships represent the sweet spot for shoppers looking to save money without sacrificing core performance, flagship cameras, or robust software suites. But given the recent price hikes across the board, their value propositions have shifted.

If your budget is dead set at under $1,000, choosing the right daily driver comes down to more than just looking at a spec sheet or briefly checking them out tethered at a carrier store. I’m breaking down where each model shines, where they fall short, and which $899 phone is truly worth buying.

Recent findings suggest that despite being the oldest contender in this lineup, launching back in the fall of 2025, the iPhone 17 remains one of the best values in Apple's catalog. It is still available due to how the organization shifted its release schedule this past September to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo first — with the iPhone 18 rumored to launch early next year alongside the iPhone 18e.

Sources indicate that when it launched, it came with an attractive $799 starting cost that I specifically noted offered one of the best bang-for-the-buck values around. But it’s since been given a $100 price hike that now puts it at $899, which is shocking considering how phones tend to get price drops a year after they’re launched — and not the other way around.

Industry observers note that still, the iPhone 17 represents the biggest leap forward for an entry-level iPhone in years over the previous iPhone 16. Apple finally ditched the sluggish 60Hz panel in favor of a buttery-smooth 120Hz ProMotion display, all while doubling the base storage to 256GB.

Recent findings suggest that apple’s A19 chip is a generation behind the latest silicon, but it hasn't missed a beat in my testing. Apps continue to launch instantaneously, and UI animations are just as fluid as ever with iOS 27, plus it handles demanding games without breaking a sweat.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Obviously, the new software brings more Apple Intelligence features and the new Siri AI. As much as I appreciate them, however, Siri still doesn’t have the same level of functionality that I get from Gemini. For example, most of its cross-app functions are limited to native apps — and not third-party ones.

In a recent development, when it comes to taking photos and video, its 48MP main camera continues to lead the way — consistently delivering crisp shots and holding its own remarkably well under low-light conditions. It’s paired with a 48MP ultrawide, but all zoom is handled by the main camera through sensor and digital cropping. As a result, it lacks the power to resolve fine details compared to its rivals.

Industry observers note that overall, I still like the iPhone 17, and it still saves you money over the $1,099 iPhone 18 Pro. Given the price hike for a year-old model, though, it’s hard to recommend at this point unless you intend on staying in the Apple ecosystem.

Just like Apple, Samsung upped the price of its base Galaxy S26 flagship model — going from $899 when it introduced this past January to a whopping $999 now. This is a tougher pill to swallow because the previous Galaxy S25 was $799, meaning there was already a $100 price hike for the S26, and it’s technically $200 more than its predecessor.

Still, it’s worth mentioning that Samsung at least doubled the base storage to 256GB. And if that’s not enough, it gets the same chip as its pricier Galaxy S26 Ultra sibling: the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy. That translates to heavyweight gaming performance and effortless multitasking on its 6.3-inch 120Hz AMOLED display, which hits a blinding 1,950 nits in our testing and remains visible under the midday sun.

According to recent reports, what makes the package more satisfying are Samsung's ambitious upcoming Agentic AI features and One UI 8.5 upgrades, including genuinely helpful additions like the new Photo Assist tools, which let me describe what photo edits I want to make on an image, and Now Nudge, which makes the phone feel more proactive in daily use. With Google Gemini on board, I’ve even used the AI to place a Dunkin’ Donuts order via DoorDash — all through a simple voice command.

I also love how the Galaxy S26 is the productivity workhorse of the trio, offering intuitive side-by-side app multitasking on the phone and greater flexibility with Samsung DeX. The latter’s really helpful because I can get a PC-like experience when I connect it to an external monitor, which isn’t something I can do with the iPhone 17.

It has been revealed that on the camera front, Samsung mostly stuck with the same triple-camera hardware as before — a 50MP main sensor, 12MP ultrawide, and 10MP telephoto with 3x optical zoom. While still photos don't represent a massive leap over last year, having a dedicated telephoto lens gives it a clear zoom advantage over the iPhone 17. For video shooters, I love the upcoming Horizon Lock video stabilization and how it keeps handheld footage dead level no matter how much I jostle or tilt the phone while shooting.

In a recent development, there are still areas for improvement with the Galaxy S26, like its shorter battery life and a boring design that has been recycled countless times with minimal changes. However, the thing that stings the most is its $999 price tag. Sure, it’s one of the most well-rounded devices here, combining compelling hardware with a superb software suite, but it’s harder to love when it's the most expensive phone in this matchup.

In a recent development, first and foremost, the Google Pixel 11 is technically the latest release out of the bunch and remains highly competitive with an $899 starting cost — up from the Pixel 10’s $799 price. At least Google softens the blow by doubling the starting storage to 256GB.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, however, the core hardware barely changes from last year. It retains a solid, durable design with a 40% thinner camera bar that sits virtually flush in a case, and its 6.3-inch Actua OLED display is remarkably bright — hitting 2,480 nits in our testing. Plus, with built-in PixelSnap charging, it matches the iPhone 17 in offering native magnetic wireless charging without the need for an add-on case.

In a recent development, where the Pixel 11 stumbles, though, is raw performance. Even though the Tensor G6 is the newest chip in this matchup, it still trails both the A19 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in benchmarks and graphics processing. Google tries to make up for it with software, rolling out genuinely useful Gemini AI features like Rambler voice dictation, Proactive Assistance, and a revamped Pixel Desktop Mode that rivals Samsung DeX when I hook it up to an external monitor.

According to recent reports, on the camera side, Google stuck with the same triple-camera hardware as before — a 48MP main sensor, 13MP ultrawide, and a 10.8MP telephoto lens. While everyday shots look nearly identical to the Pixel 10, having a dedicated 5x optical zoom gives it the strongest zoom performance in this trio, effortlessly outreaching the Galaxy S26's 3x lens and the iPhone 17's digital crop.

According to recent reports, new camera tools that I appreciate include Magic Capture, which leans on AI to pick out picture-perfect shots for me so I can remain immersed in the moment. Another helpful tool, Creator Suite, makes it even easier to vlog and record selfie videos thanks to a built-in teleprompter. The Pixel 11 isn’t perfect, but its $899 price tag makes it hard to resist.

Delta-E color accuracy (lower is better).

122.3 (Adaptive) / 106.9 (Natural).

86.6 (Adaptive) / 75.7 (Natural).

0.24 (Adaptive) / 0.21 (Natural).

Recent findings suggest that all three phones feature crisp 6.3-inch displays with up to a 120Hz refresh rate, making them equally smooth for scrolling and gaming. However, our lab testing reveals a huge gap in peak brightness. The Pixel 11 easily takes the crown at 2,480 nits, noticeably outshining the Galaxy S26 at 1,950 nits and leaving the iPhone 17 trailing at 1,505 nits.

Under direct sunlight, the Pixel 11 is far easier to read without forcing me to shade it with my hand, whereas the iPhone 17 can look significantly dimmer by comparison.

Geekbench 6 (single-core/multi-core).

3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited (score/fps).

Recent findings suggest that personally, I think all three phones feel snappy enough for everyday tasks such as browsing, streaming, and jumping between apps. Our benchmark testing, however, demonstrates a clear powerhouse amongst the trio.

The Galaxy S26’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 takes the overall performance crown, leading the pack in Geekbench 6 multi-core testing with a score of 10,778 and dominating graphics with 28,548 (171.6 fps) in 3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited. The iPhone 17’s older A19 chip holds its own remarkably well, while the Pixel 11’s Tensor G6 regrettably falls behind despite being the newest silicon in this trio.

This doesn't mean the Pixel 11 feels sluggish in casual tasks, but if you play graphics-intensive games or push your phone with heavy video editing, the Galaxy S26 and iPhone 17 give you better sustained performance.

Average Battery life (Hrs:Mins).

When it comes to battery endurance, the iPhone 17 and Pixel 11 are virtually neck and neck, while the Galaxy S26 trails behind. In our battery benchmark test, the iPhone 17 edges out the win at 12 hours and 47 minutes, closely followed by the Pixel 11 at 12 hours and 45 minutes. Meanwhile, the Galaxy S26 lags more than an hour behind at 11 hours and 28 minutes.

The iPhone 17 widens its lead when it’s time to plug in as well. In fact, it reaches 39% in 15 minutes and 71% after 30 minutes of wired charging. By comparison, the Galaxy S26 hits 29% at the 15-minute mark and 57% in 30 minutes, while the Pixel 11 gets to 27% and 52%, respectively.

After putting them through their paces, I would actually recommend buying the Google Pixel 11. Price hikes across the board make these phones a tougher value proposition than they used to be, but the Pixel 11 delivers the most well-rounded experience for the money.

It has been revealed that it’s not the fastest phone on paper, nor does it charge the quickest. However, it easily outshines the competition with the brightest display in direct sunlight, solid real-world all-day battery life, and the most versatile camera system, thanks to its dedicated 5x optical zoom and genuinely useful Creator Suite tools.

Throw in built-in PixelSnap magnetic charging, Pixel Desktop Mode, and the smartest Gemini AI features at my disposal, and the Pixel 11 gives you the best bang for your buck without forcing you to spend over $1,000.

John’s a senior editor covering phones for Tom’s Guide. He’s no stranger in this area having covered mobile phones and gadgets since 2008 when he started his career. On top of his editor duties, he’s a seasoned videographer being in front and behind the camera producing YouTube videos. Previously, he held editor roles with PhoneArena, Android Authority, Digital Trends, and SPY. Outside of tech, he enjoys producing mini documentaries and fun social clips for small businesses, enjoying the beach life at the Jersey Shore, and recently becoming a first time homeowner.

  • Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.
  • Salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents.
  • In a recent development, brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

Salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

In a recent development, brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Sources indicate that retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

In a recent development, shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

According to recent reports, 1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

The survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

Sources indicate that agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent people using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

The majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

Retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

It has been revealed that today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

Tech Report: What to Buy (and Skip) on Black Friday 2026

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1063 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
  • If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
  • It has been revealed that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The major day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

It has been revealed that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, claims Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

Non-electronic toys are a good bet, claims Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

NeeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold notes.

While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

In a recent development, “Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley claims.

According to recent reports, got some counter space and an itch for a fresh food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

“Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath notes. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold says.

It has been revealed that electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath states.

Gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath says. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

That said, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold claims.

For best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, notes consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after Newly introduced Year’s Day.

“Big-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold claims.

Many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath states. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

It has been revealed that shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold states. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

Recent findings suggest that just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath says. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

Sources indicate that one caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch says. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

It has been revealed that fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch says.

Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

Let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch indicates. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

Check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley indicates. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

Industry observers note that use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

Addas a preferred source on Google.

If you use an AI chatbot and you’re concerned about your privacy and the personal information it ingests, you can do something about it. While Claude — our top pick for AI chatbots — is one of the better options when it comes to privacy, the default settings can still leave something to be desired if you value yours.

Luckily, you can mitigate or even eliminate the amount of data Claude knows about you, as long as you know where to look.

From having Claude train on your conversations to track your location and more, here are a series of settings you should consider changing if you want to stay on top of your privacy when using one of the best AI chatbots around.

It has been revealed that by default, most AI chatbots have a setting on by default that allows them to be trained on the conversations you have. This is the first and likely the most vital setting you need to disable. Here’s how to turn it off.

While you’re at it, if you’re a Claude Code user, these settings will let you delete Code sessions stored on Anthropic’s server without deleting local sessions on your computer.

If you’ve ever shared a chat with anyone, you can also delete those chats in this menu as well.

Read More: Keep Your Data Yours: How to Opt Out of AI Chatbot Training.

Anthropic will use your location when using Claude to “improve product experience.” It will use your device’s IP address to identify your city and region, but you can disable this setting — to some extent. How you go about doing this will depend on what device you’re using to access Claude.

In a recent development, according to the support article, if you’re using the mobile app (iOS or Android) or the web extension, the location settings are located within the device’s settings and not the Claude app settings. However, I found two ways to do this on Android. (See below.).

The Claude app will not request access to your location unless your prompt has a specific location-based query, like “What are some of the best sushi restaurants around me?” Only then will the app request permission.

However, if you already have given Claude access on Android or iOS, here’s how you can revoke permission.

I was surprised to see a section in the Settings of the Android app that I didn’t see on iOS, but it will also allow you to disable your location right from the app.

One thing to keep in mind is that turning your location off can affect features like searches that require your location, but Anthropic explicitly states that it collects your IP address to infer coarse-grained location to ensure usage of Claude complies with its terms and to prevent abuse — despite questionable allegations.

Industry observers note that like other AI chatbots, Claude has built-in “memory” so it can more easily have context about your conversations. Memory is on by default: The chatbot will remember personal preferences and other information and will be able to take that into consideration in other conversations, even if you don’t explicitly mention it in your current session.

Sources indicate that if you’d prefer a clean slate, you can ask in the chat what memories it has collected about you and then tell Claude to delete specific memories or all of them. However, there’s a dedicated section in the settings to help you view and manage memories directly.

In the web version of Claude, do the following to access your memory settings:.

In a recent development, this will display all stored memories Claude has for you. You can edit a specific memory to your liking by clicking on the pencil icon on the right side of the memory or delete it entirely by clicking on the trash icon.

To prevent Claude from creating upcoming memories from your conversations:.

Recent findings suggest that if you have had conversations with Claude that were sensitive in nature and still had the “Help improve our AI models” option enabled, odds are that Anthropic has already trained Claude on that conversation. There’s no way to change that.

According to recent reports, however, you should find those conversations in your chat history and delete them. After you’ve done that and disabled AI training on your conversations, you should opt for incognito mode for any further sensitive conversations you might want to have going forward.

Incognito chats aren’t saved in your history, nor are they used to train models.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

According to recent reports, if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The firm already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Recent findings suggest that abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro blueprint, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

In a recent development, at launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg noted Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent owners may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Industry observers note that also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

Industry observers note that as with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

The feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US owners can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

The change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The new landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

It has been revealed that “Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

According to recent reports, also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

“You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release said. Google’s latest Memory summary feature for Gemini lets owners view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

Industry observers note that apple is kicking off a newly introduced and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful fresh features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

First up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

Sources indicate that A new feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

In a recent development, with a new feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

It has been revealed that the new app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

Normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the latest Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

Sources indicate that some of the new features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone customers. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

Latest Update: Meta’s Carbon Emissions Went Up 45% Last Year. AI Is Making It Worse

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (421 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used.
  • In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the manufacturer is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.
  • It has been revealed that it’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used. But like every Big Tech company, Meta is sacrificing its climate goals for artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it.

In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the manufacturer is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.

It has been revealed that it’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement. Microsoft, Amazon and Google have also all backtracked on their climate goals in their rush to build hyperscale data centers, the turbocharged server farms needed to keep AI online. Microsoft’s president, Brad Smith, said in 2023 that the tech giant’s net zero goal was “before the explosion in artificial intelligence.”.

Meta’s net emissions in 2025 were 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, a 45% increase year over year, the company indicates. Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are primary drivers of the climate crisis, worsening natural disasters, causing more extreme weather patterns and disrupting the lives of everyone and everything on the planet.

Take one of Meta’s Louisiana data centers, Hyperion, for example. CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the behemoth in 2025, showing how the facility is nearly the size of Manhattan. When it comes online in 2030, it’s expected to create two gigawatts of capacity for AI, with the ability to scale in the future. But it also requires equally massive demands on the state’s energy grid.

If you're here looking for lower mortgage interest rates, today is definitely not your day.

This is 25 basis points higher than yesterday and 12 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

Keep in mind that mortgage rates are always on the move, and that if you're tracking rates day-to-day, you're going to see a lot of volatility. Zooming out and looking at the bigger picture — like a graph showing at least a month's worth of rate data — can help you see the overall trend.

According to recent reports, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

In a recent development, investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there aren’t many people for whom that’s true.

Sources indicate that also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

It has been revealed that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a upcoming home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

In a recent development, if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • The newly introduced Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the new Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

The newly introduced Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app people on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the latest Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

In a recent development, agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

  • It has been revealed that I enjoyed my day of digital DIY significantly more than becoming the city’s most wanted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The day before Grand Theft Auto 6’s launch, like many gamers, I returned to Grand Theft Auto 5’s Los Santos for one last ride. Within moments of booting up my multi-hundred-hour save, I was causing chaos with a bazooka before switching to a devastating portable mini-gun. It was the stuff of pure GTA carnage; extreme violence, utterly gleeful in its sheer absurdity.

The next day, I spent the majority of my first hour with GTA 6, trying to decide what color to paint the protagonist’s bedroom walls, fixing the leaky roof, and replacing rotting wooden planks on a staircase, before unwinding by shooting some hoops in my front yard and going for a gentle kayak. I’d swapped being a one-man army for being a domesticated virtual boyfriend.

It has been revealed that I enjoyed my day of digital DIY significantly more than becoming the city’s most wanted. And that’s what makes GTA 6 a game-changer. It has literally changed the way I game. If previous Grand Theft Autos were sprawling sandboxes, ripe for wanton destruction, GTA 6’s Vice City is the first Rockstar Games world I don’t want to destroy; I just want to exist in.

Industry observers note that after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived. Set in the state of Leonida, with Vice City at its heart, you play Jason and Lucia, two criminals forced into an increasingly dangerous situation as they seek their fortune, discovering the darker side of the sunniest spot in America.

GTA 6 is still a Grand Theft Auto game, so the option to go on a rampage is very much present. If you want to play your Jason and/or Lucia as a murderous psychopath that robs every gas station they find, terrorizes ordinary citizens, and is hunted by the Vice City Police Department, Rockstar Games won’t stop you (though such criminal actions will be reflected in your “Criminal Profile,” which reportedly has narrative consequences).

Sources indicate that much to my surprise, I just haven’t felt the desire to engage in random acts of violence. Instead, I’ve been content to take my time, observing the world at a slower pace as a law-abiding citizen. I’ve even been obeying traffic laws!

But much to my surprise, as noted above, unlike in GTA 5, I just haven’t felt the desire to engage in random acts of violence. Instead, for the majority of my five hours with the game so far (a playtime that should swell significantly over the weekend), I’ve been content to take my time, observing the world at a slower pace as a law-abiding citizen. I’ve even been obeying traffic laws!

Recent findings suggest that the DNA of Red Dead Redemption 2 has most definitely bled into GTA, and in my book, that’s a very good thing. Like that 2018 masterpiece, actions in GTA feel deliberate, and the level of detail in environments and how you can interact with the world is staggering. I can’t think of another AAA game that has made me want to work out, wolf down a protein bar, and take a shower afterwards. It’s not so much digital escapism as living a virtual second life.

According to recent reports, I’m typically a goal-oriented player; I like having something to do at all times. Which means with a lot of games, I find myself mission-hopping, neglecting to enjoy the setting in the process. With GTA 6, I’ve done the exact opposite. I’ve barely made any story progress, because I’ve been losing myself in Jason’s local neighborhood, pottering around shops, sitting by the beach drinking a smoothie, or taking to the ocean to see what sea life I can find.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Industry observers note that the reason for my change in approach is probably that GTA 6 looks absolutely incredible on PS5 Pro. Yes, the 30 fps cap is disappointing, but the visual quality makes up for it. When an open-world setting looks this stunning and is rendered in such rich detail, perhaps it’s only natural to want to experience it as a real human would, rather than viewing it as a sandbox.

Maybe at some point, I’ll get bored of just existing in Leonaida (and I haven’t even been to Vice City yet), and then I’ll be glad to have the story missions to funnel me through over-the-top action set pieces. But at this early stage in my playthrough, the biggest joy that GTA 6 has brought me hasn’t been from stealing cars or robbing convenience stores, but just taking a lazy stroll.
